questions.q: What is a Virtual Machine Scale Set (VMSS)?
options: A group of identical VM instances deployed and managed as a single resource, typically behind a load balancer
A single large VM with more CPU cores than normal
A billing construct with no actual compute resources
A tool for resizing one VM's disk
questions.explain: A VMSS lets you deploy and manage a group of identical, load-balanced VM instances as one resource instead of creating them individually.

questions.q: What metric does a typical autoscale rule most commonly watch to decide when to scale out?
options: CPU percentage
The VM's admin username
The number of resource groups in the subscription
The VM's region name
questions.explain: Autoscale rules commonly watch CPU percentage (though memory or custom metrics work too), scaling out when it crosses a defined threshold.

questions.q: In the rule "Percentage CPU > 70 avg 10m, scale out 1", what does this rule actually do?
options: Deletes an instance whenever CPU drops below 70%
Adds one instance when average CPU exceeds 70% over a 10-minute window
Changes the VM size to a larger one
Does nothing unless manually triggered
questions.explain: This rule scales the set out by one instance when average CPU has exceeded 70% for 10 minutes.

questions.q: Why does setting a minimum and maximum instance count matter for an autoscaled Scale Set?
options: It has no real effect and is optional in every case
It keeps the set from shrinking below what availability requires or growing past a cost ceiling
It determines which Azure region the set deploys to
It controls which OS image the instances use
questions.explain: Min and max instance counts bound autoscale on both ends, protecting availability on the low end and cost on the high end.

questions.q: Why does a Scale Set with autoscale handle variable, spiky traffic better than a fixed number of always-on VMs sized for peak load?
options: It doesn't — fixed capacity is always better
It runs only the minimum needed capacity during quiet periods and adds instances automatically when load actually increases, then removes them again afterward
Because Scale Sets are immune to CPU load entirely
Because autoscale eliminates the need for a load balancer
questions.explain: Autoscale avoids paying for peak-sized capacity around the clock while still being able to grow automatically within minutes when real demand increases.
